meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'scam, swindle, fraudulent scheme' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: His caviar scam fell through.

examples.trans: If your scam surfaces, they will simply kill you!
That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.
How is it in Hungary?

Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'lucky person, lucky dog' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You got lucky, you are a real lucky guy.

examples.text: А если не всплывёт, ты настоящий везунчик.

Share with everyone.

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment

examples.trans: Bad timing!
He always comes on time.

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.en: to surface, emerge, come to light
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'плыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to surface, come to light', paired with 'всплывать'.

examples.text: Обман может всплыть в любой момент.
examples.trans: Deception can come to light at any moment.

examples.text: Если твоя афера всплывёт, тебя просто убьют!
examples.trans: If your scam surfaces, they will simply kill you!

examples.text: А если не всплывёт, ты настоящий везунчик.
examples.trans: And if it does not surface, you are a real lucky guy.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you

examples.trans: That's what you said.
I speak Russian.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Even a child knows.
Even Mum doesn't know.
Yes! Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'two hundred' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Двести десять на сто тридцать девять!
examples.trans: Two hundred and ten over one hundred and thirty-nine!
Two hundred rubles.

examples.text: С тебя ровно двести тысяч рублей прямо сейчас.
examples.trans: That will be exactly two hundred thousand rubles right now.

достать.gloss: to take out, to get, to reach

meanings.en: to take out, to pull out, to reach
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

meanings.en: to get hold of, to obtain

examples.trans: And take his eye out with a spoon.
He took his phone out of his pocket.

examples.text: Вы понимаете, что вы нас достали уже?
examples.trans: Do you understand that you've made us sick of you already?

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.trans: Come if you want.
And if not?
Take her if you want.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.
I want to live normally.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.en: to bury in the ground; figuratively to ruin oneself
meanings.note: закопать себя = to dig one's own grave / ruin oneself

examples.trans: Samsonov is finished, he buried himself.
The dog buried a bone in the garden.

examples.text: Что вы так переживаете? Самсонов всё, он себя закопал.
examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that? Samsonov is finished, he buried himself.

meanings.note: жить на зарплату = to live on one's salary

examples.trans: He lives on his salary.
He has a good salary.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович учёный, и он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich is a scholar, and he lives on a salary.

злить.gloss: to anger, to irritate, to infuriate

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to anger, to irritate, to infuriate', paired with 'разозлить'.

examples.trans: Do not anger the chef today.
This situation angers me.
The main thing is not to anger the chef.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Смотри, дядя Даня, видишь, побелел! Испугался он зимнего леса.
examples.trans: Look, Uncle Danya has gone pale, see! He is afraid of the winter forest.

meanings.note: уже месяц = for a month now

examples.trans: They will bury you in a grave.

examples.text: Я даже не буду плакать на могиле.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.

Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.
It's a decent job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.
It was an ordinary day.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.
She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cry, to weep', paired with 'заплакать'.

examples.trans: Please don't cry.

examples.text: Да, мы покрасим всю эту икру.

Give me some useful advice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm tired, so I'm at home.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm just tired.

examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.

I mean it.
No way, what, seriously?
Understood, chef!
Understood, chef! I will find the knife.

examples.text: Слушаюсь, шеф, я сделаю всё моментально.
examples.trans: Understood, chef, I will do everything instantly.

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.
This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.note: 'а то' at the start of a sentence: 'а то мы уже начали беспокоиться' = we were starting to worry

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: We were starting to worry, you see.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A thousand roubles.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: 'mum will kill me' = I'll be in big trouble

examples.trans: Do you want to kill me?
I'll kill you! (said in anger)

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович учёный, и он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich is a scholar, and he lives on a salary.

examples.text: Учёные говорят, что она даже полезнее чёрной!
examples.trans: Scientists say it is even healthier than black!

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.
We waited for a whole hour.

examples.text: Илья Олегович! Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: Ilya Olegovich! I can't walk around here all day.
What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!
Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.en: to fine, penalize, impose a fine on
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fine, penalize', paired with 'оштрафовать'.

examples.trans: The director fines the dishonest cook.

examples.text: Я штрафую тебя на двести тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: I am fining you two hundred thousand rubles.

examples.text: Щучья икра очень вкусная и полезная.
examples.trans: Pike roe is very tasty and healthy.

examples.text: Это отличная щучья икра, пять килограммов.
examples.trans: This is excellent pike caviar, five kilograms.

examples.text: Щучья икра всегда бывает жёлтого цвета.
examples.trans: Pike caviar is always yellow in color.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
